summary: Full-stack testing of 'Ma Maison' (My Home) feature completed. Backend: 27/27 pytest tests passing (properties CRUD + cascade delete, equipment CRUD, documents CRUD, reminders CRUD with auto-due flag, timeline aggregation + sort desc + grouped by year, insights with demo_values fallback, 6 AI cards coming_soon, auth guards 401/404). Frontend (mobile 390x844): login OK, 'Ma Maison' tab visible in bottom nav, list shows existing property with counters, dashboard shows hero+quick actions+insights (100%, 6 interventions, 3240€)+entretiens vides+équipements récents vides+6 cartes IA BIENTÔT. Sub-screens (equipment, documents, timeline, insights, reminders, create) render correctly with proper empty states. Modal-based creation flows verified end-to-end: created equipment 'UI_TEST_Chaudière' and reminder 'UI_TEST_Rappel' via UI → both persisted and displayed. Test data cleaned up.

minor.issue: PATCH acts as PUT — the endpoint calls body.dict() on EquipmentInput/PropertyInput which reintroduces default None values for optional fields not sent by the client (e.g. installed_on, warranty_until, year_built). This nulls out previously-saved data if the client omits a field. Consider Pydantic model_dump(exclude_unset=True) or a dedicated partial-update model. Server: /app/backend/server.py:1229 (property update) and :1299 (equipment update).

issues: Runtime warnings in web preview: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow"' and 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Harmless on native, but noisy in web preview. Consider updating helper style utils.

action_items: (Optional / minor) Fix PATCH semantics so partial updates don't wipe optional fields (use exclude_unset=True or a separate PropertyUpdate/EquipmentUpdate model). Not blocking — the frontend currently sends full payloads.
(Optional) Silence RN-Web deprecation warnings for shadow* and pointerEvents in shared style helpers.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1509 lines — approaching the 700-line threshold; consider splitting My Home routes into a dedicated router module (properties.py, equipment.py, etc.).
PATCH endpoints use full input schema (EquipmentInput/PropertyInput) which forces clients to send all fields to avoid data loss. Prefer partial-update patterns.
All /properties routes correctly enforce ownership via _get_property() — no leakage across users (verified with 404 test).
Insights demo_values fallback works as documented (money=3240, interventions=6 when everything empty).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all screens render + creation flows verified end-to-end)

seed_data_creation: Used existing test client (client.test@auxora.fr) and existing property prop_b0858d7dc142. Test-created equipment/reminders/documents/properties were all cleaned up (TEST_/UI_TEST_ prefix + explicit teardown).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Ma Maison feature is fully operational. Backend endpoints under /api/properties/** are covered by /app/backend/tests/test_my_home.py. Frontend flows tested: Ma Maison tab → property card → dashboard → equipment/documents/timeline/insights/reminders/create. Modal-based create for equipment and reminders both persist correctly. Only nit is that PATCH endpoints act like PUT (default-None fields overwrite existing data).
rca_of_issue: No blocking issue. PATCH-as-PUT behavior detailed in backend_issues.minor: the server does `updates = body.dict()` on Pydantic input models with optional defaults set to None, which then overwrites saved values. Fix: `updates = body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` or introduce partial-update schemas.
